10.title: How the GOV.UK Content API works
10.content:
How the GOV.UK Content API works This page explains how the GOV.UK Content API represents GOV.UK content and describes the data it returns. The GOV.UK Content API is a public, read-only API that provides access to the content and metadata for supported pages on the GOV.UK website as JSON. What the GOV.UK Content API returns A successful request to the GOV.UK Content API returns a JSON response representing a piece of content, conforming to the ContentItem schema. You can retrieve this data for a supported GOV.UK page by including the page’s path in a request to the GOV.UK Content API. For example, for the VAT rates page: curl https://www.gov.uk/api/content/vat-rates The response contains fields for the content itself, its metadata and its relationships with other GOV.UK content. The following sections explain the purpose of the key fields in the response and what their values mean. Base paths { ... "base_path": "/vat-rates", ... } Every successful API response has a base_path field. This field always has the same value as the path parameter used to identify the content in the API request. This is called the base path because it is the canonical path to the piece of content. Some pieces of content may appear on multiple pages on the GOV.UK website. Document types and schema names { ... "document_type": "answer", "schema_name": "answer", ... } The document_type and schema_name fields are used to describe the type and structure of data returned for a piece of content: document_type: specifies the type of content represented by the response. This field typically indicates how the piece of content is used on the GOV.UK website. schema_name: refers to a JSON schema file held in GOV.UK Content Schemas. This schema defines the structure of the object in the response’s details field. Often the document_type and schema_name fields share the same value. In the VAT rates example, both fields have value answer. The document_type and schema_name can also have different values, because multiple document types can conform to the same schema. This allows pieces of content with the same data structure to serve different purposes on GOV.UK. The values of document_type and schema_name affect the details and links fields. The following sections explain these effects. Details { ... "details": { "body": "\n
\n

The standard VAT rate...", "external_related_links": [] }, ... } (The body in this example has been shortened for presentation here.) The details field in an API response is an object that contains data in an appropriate structure for the piece of content. This structure is defined by the JSON schema identified in the schema_name field. In the VAT rates example, the answer schema is used. This answer schema specifies the following for the details field: a body field, which contains the HTML for the main body of the piece of content. an external_related_links field containing links to related web pages outside the GOV.UK website. Links { ... "links": { ... "organisations": [ { "analytics_identifier": "D25", "api_path": "/api/content/government/organisations/hm-revenue-customs", "api_url": "https://www.gov.uk/api/content/government/organisations/hm-revenue-customs", "base_path": "/government/organisations/hm-revenue-customs", "content_id": "6667cce2-e809-4e21-ae09-cb0bdc1ddda3", "details": { "acronym": "HMRC", "brand": "hm-revenue-customs", ... "organisation_govuk_status": { "status": "live", "updated_at": null, "url": null } }, "document_type": "organisation", "links": {}, "locale": "en", "schema_name": "organisation", "title": "HM Revenue & Customs", "web_url": "https://www.gov.uk/government/organisations/hm-revenue-customs", "withdrawn": false } ], ... }, ... } The links field in an API response is used to describe relationships between the piece of content represented, and other GOV.UK content. This field is an object in which each key identifies a type of content relationship. The content schema identified by the schema_name field defines which link types can appear as keys in the links object. The value associated with each key is an array of objects representing related pieces of content of that type. Each object in the array conforms to the LinkedContentItem schema, containing the fields needed to express the content relationship. This may itself include a links field, allowing content relationships to be nested. You can use nested links fields and the parent link type to show a hierarchy of content in your application or service. Although these relationships are called links, they are not necessarily presented as HTML links when the content is rendered on the GOV.UK website. For example, in the VAT rates response, the organisations link type identifies the government organisations related to the piece of content. You can use this data to retrieve other content published by those organisations, such as news or guidance. HTML in responses Some fields in the API response, such as the body of the details object, may contain content formatted using Govspeak. Govspeak is a simplified Markdown syntax developed for GOV.UK. The GOV.UK Content API converts this Govspeak into HTML before returning it in the response. This means you can render the content in your application with its intended structure, such as headings, lists and links, without needing to implement your own Govspeak parser. The API response does not return CSS with this HTML, so you must provide the CSS needed to style the content in your application or service. Content states and paths Canonical paths and redirects A single piece of content served by the GOV.UK Content API can be used to render multiple pages on the GOV.UK website. For example, the local laws and customs for Thailand are available as a standalone page, and also as one part of a printable guide. The canonical path to the piece of content for both of these pages is /foreign-travel-advice/thailand, and you can retrieve this content using the GOV.UK Content API. If you request this piece of content using the path to the standalone page /foreign-travel-advice/thailand/local-laws-and-customs, the API returns a 303 HTTP status code redirecting you to the canonical path. $ curl -I https://www.gov.uk/api/content/foreign-travel-advice/thailand/local-laws-and-customs HTTP/1.1 303 See Other ... Location: https://www.gov.uk/api/content/foreign-travel-advice/thailand ... Withdrawn content { ... "withdrawn_notice": { "explanation": "

This document is out of date. See the current complete routine immunisation schedule.

\n
", "withdrawn_at": "2015-08-12T13:47:11Z" } ... } Some content on the GOV.UK website provides information that is no longer applicable, but remains available for reference. This content is described as withdrawn. Withdrawn content is displayed on the GOV.UK website with a header describing its status. For example, The complete routine immunisation schedule 2013 to 2014 was withdrawn because the content became out of date. In a response from the GOV.UK Content API for a piece of withdrawn content, this status is indicated using the withdrawn_notice field. Next steps Now that you understand how the GOV.UK Content API represents a piece of content, you can: retrieve and display GOV.UK content look up specific data from the API response

11.title: Get started
11.content:
Get started
This guide walks you through using the GOV.UK Content API for the first time.
You can use this guide if you are a developer or a non-developer who understands
the basics of APIs. You’ll retrieve GOV.UK content by making a GET
request to the API, which returns the content as JSON.
Before you start
Make sure you have one of the following tools:


a terminal with a data transfer utility, such as curl
a web browser, such as Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge or Firefox

Authentication
You do not need to authenticate or include any custom HTTP headers to use the
GOV.UK Content API.
Base URL
The base URL for all requests to the GOV.UK Content API is:
https://www.gov.uk/api/content/
Make your first API request
To make your first request to the GOV.UK Content API:


Choose a page on the GOV.UK website, for example https://www.gov.uk/take-pet-abroad.
Make a note of the URL component after the domain, which for our example is:
/take-pet-abroad.
This URL component is the path that you will send to the API.
Add this path to the end of the API’s base URL: https://www.gov.uk/api/content/take-pet-abroad
Using your preferred tool, make a GET request to the resulting URL. For example,
with the curl utility in your terminal:
curl https://www.gov.uk/api/content/take-pet-abroad
Alternatively, you can use your web browser to make the GET request. Navigate
to the API URL by entering it in your browser’s address bar.

You get a JSON response containing the GOV.UK content and metadata. The fields
contained in this response are explained in the API reference.
Next steps
Now that you’ve made your first API request, you can:


learn how the GOV.UK Content API works
retrieve and display GOV.UK content

12.title: API reference
12.content:
GOV.UK Content API v1.0.0
GOV.UK Content API provides a simple and consistent way to request
GOV.UK content as structured data in a predictable
format. It is used within the GOV.UK website as the means for applications
to lookup content in order to render it.
This API accepts HTTP requests and responds with
JSON data containing the same
published content as is presented on GOV.UK.




  Servers
  
    
    
    https://www.gov.uk/api/content
  
  



/{path}

get

  Lookup GOV.UK content by path


  This is the primary interface to lookup the content required to render
a page on GOV.UK
It accepts an input of the path of the page you are looking up. For
example, if you were looking up travel advice for Thailand which is
hosted on GOV.UK at https://www.gov.uk/foreign-travel-advice/thailand
you would make a request to
https://www.gov.uk/api/content/foreign-travel-advice/thailand.
If the content is available at the requested path you will receive
a ContentItem containing the structured data
for that page.
In the GOV.UK context, content schemas are structured rules that define
what a specific type of content can contain and how it’s organised.
Think of them as a strict blueprint or a template for every piece of
information published on GOV.UK. These schemas ensure that all content
is consistent, predictable, and machine-readable.
Each schema is a formal definition, written in JSON Schema, that
specifies the underlying structure for a content type. For example, a
schema for a “News Article” would define all the possible fields for
that article, such as:


title: A mandatory text field with a maximum character limit.
summary: A mandatory short description.
body: The main content of the article, which itself must conform
to the rules of Govspeak (GOV.UK’s version of Markdown).
publication_date: A mandatory field that must be in a valid date
format.
image: An optional field that must contain specific sub-fields like
a URL and alt text.
related_links: A list where each item must have a title and a URL.

By enforcing these rules, schemas guarantee that every news article
across GOV.UK has the same fundamental structure.

Rate limiting
There is a maximum limit of 10 requests per second per client. If you exceed
this your request won’t be processed until the limit is no longer exceeded
and you may see timeout errors.
We think this should be sufficient for all users of GOV.UK Content API but
if you believe you need the limit increasing you can contact support.

13.title: Security and compliance
13.content:
Security and compliance
HTTPS
GOV.UK Content API follows government HTTPS security guidelines. The
Hypertext Transfer Protocol Secure (HTTPS), which involves the Transport Layer
Security (TLS) protocol, is used by the platform to provide secure connections.
Security patches
We treat security vulnerabilities in the platform and library code in the GOV.UK
Content API as our highest priority. The codebase will be updated as soon as
possible when vulnerabilities are discovered or reported.
We frequently upgrade the framework and library code in GOV.UK Content API
to the latest versions for security and feature enhancements.
Report vulnerabilities
If you believe there is a security issue with GOV.UK Content API, read our security
policy
and contact us immediately.
Please don’t disclose the suspected breach publicly until it has been fixed.

14.title: GOV.UK Content API
14.content:
GOV.UK Content API
The GOV.UK Content API is a public, read-only API for retrieving content and metadata
from supported pages on the GOV.UK website. This information is available
to any member of the public, but the API provides it in a format that your services,
tools and products can consume directly.
This technical documentation gives you information on:


how the GOV.UK Content API works
what you can and cannot use the API for
how to retrieve and display GOV.UK content

Contact us if you have any questions or feedback.
What you can do with this API
You can use the GOV.UK Content API for building services, tools and products which
incorporate content from GOV.UK, and for keeping that content up to date.
The GOV.UK Content API returns a JSON representation of a live page
from the GOV.UK website. The response includes page metadata, links to
related content, and the page body as HTML. This provides a more convenient and
predictable interface than scraping the HTML from web pages.
The information returned by the API includes links between related GOV.UK content.
For example, a response may identify the government organisation that published
a page. You could then retrieve that organisation’s policies from another page.
Our API reference describes the API endpoints and response format
a developer can expect.
What you cannot do with this API
The content and metadata you can access using the GOV.UK Content API are limited
to live pages on the GOV.UK website, published on the www.gov.uk domain.
For example, here are some pages that you can access using the API:


Holiday entitlement rights on www.gov.uk
Registering for Self Assessment on www.gov.uk
Pay and conditions on www.gov.uk

The GOV.UK Content API does not provide access to content from websites on other
subdomains of gov.uk, such as blog.gov.uk. The following are examples of pages
that you cannot access using the API:


Transforming towns and cities for people and nature on blog.gov.uk
Using GOV.UK Pay on payments.service.gov.uk

You also cannot use this API to search GOV.UK content, or use any filters
such as date, type, or page relationship. You can only retrieve content by path,
as described in Get started.
If you want to search or filter for GOV.UK content before retrieving it, use the
GOV.UK Search API.
Types of content available from this API
Some fields in the API response from the GOV.UK Content API contain HTML. This
HTML may reference images, attachments or other files, but you cannot use the API
to return those files directly. Instead you must retrieve, for example, a referenced
image file directly from its source by other means.
In addition, you can only access content from static pages on the GOV.UK website
using this API. Content from dynamic pages (for example, from a search, or using
data that changes over time) is not available from this API.
Some types of content are still being migrated to the GOV.UK Content API. In such
cases, you may encounter a placeholder page which holds no content, or a redirect
to a catch-all destination for unmigrated content. You can find more information
in the API reference.
You cannot access historic content using this API. If you want to access historic
content, you can get this from the UK Government Web Archive.
Who can use this API
The GOV.UK Content API is public, and anyone can use it. You do not need to seek
permission or sign any agreements to use this API.

18.title: Retrieve and display GOV.UK content
18.content:
Retrieve and display GOV.UK content The example below illustrates utilising Ruby on Rails with Rest Client to make use of GOV.UK in your application. require "rest-client" tax_help = Rails.cache.fetch("govuk/tax-help", expires_in: 1.hour) do response = RestClient.get("https://www.gov.uk/api/content/tax-help", { content_type: "json" }) JSON.parse(response.body).dig("details", "body") end content = "

GOV.UK Tax Help

#{tax_help}
" In this example we utilise the Rails cache layer so that we can infrequently access the content without concerns of hitting the rate limit. We then use the API to access the content for Tax Help. In the response we access the body field from within the details object. We store this to a variable tax_help. Finally we embed this in our own HTML and are ready to output to users.

19.title: Accessibility statement for GOV.UK Content API documentation
19.content:
Accessibility statement for GOV.UK Content API documentation
This accessibility statement applies to the GOV.UK Content API documentation at
https://content-api.publishing.service.gov.uk/.
This website is run by the GOV.UK developer team at the Government Digital
Service (GDS). We want as many people as possible to be able to use this
website. For example, that means you should be able to:


change colours, contrast levels and fonts
zoom in up to 300% without the text spilling off the screen
navigate most of the website using just a keyboard
navigate most of the website using speech recognition software
listen to most of the website using a screen reader (including the most recent
versions of JAWS, NVDA and VoiceOver)

We’ve also made the website text as simple as possible to understand.
AbilityNet has advice on making your device
easier to use if you have a disability.
How accessible this website is
We know some parts of this website are not fully accessible as there are issues
caused by our Technical Documentation Template.
Feedback and contact information
If you need any part of this service in a different format like large print,
audio recording or braille, contact us using the GOV.UK contact form.
We’ll consider your request and get back to you within 3 working days.
Reporting accessibility problems with this website
We’re always looking to improve the accessibility of this website. If you find
any problems not listed on this page or think we’re not meeting accessibility
requirements, contact us using the GOV.UK contact form.
Enforcement procedure
The Equality and Human Rights Commission (EHRC) is responsible for enforcing the
Public Sector Bodies (Websites and Mobile Applications) (No. 2) Accessibility
Regulations 2018 (the ‘accessibility regulations’). If you’re not happy with how
we respond to your complaint, contact the Equality Advisory and Support Service
(EASS).
Technical information about this website’s accessibility
GDS is committed to making its website accessible, in accordance with the Public
Sector Bodies (Websites and Mobile Applications) (No. 2) Accessibility
Regulations 2018.
Non-compliance with the accessibility regulations
Some parts of this website are not fully accessible because of issues caused by
our Technical Documentation Template.
Preparation of this accessibility statement
This statement was prepared on 2 September 2020. It was last reviewed on 30 June
2021.
This website was last tested in August 2020. The test was carried out by the
technical writing team at GDS. We used the WAVE Web Accessibility Evaluation
Tool and a checklist we created with the help of the
GDS accessibility team. We tested all the website’s pages.
